text.title: ui-ux-design.md Template Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every per-feature ui-ux-design.md MUST satisfy: when it is required and how a skip is recorded, the exact five Nielsen rows, the two Norman principles (affordance, feedback), the six sections in fixed order and the load-bearing States table. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: If the feature renders or modifies any visible element on a listed surface — web UI (page, component, form, button, modal, navigation), mobile UI (screen, sheet, gesture handler), CLI TUI (interactive prompt, picker, dashboard view) — ui-ux-design.md MUST exist.
rule.rationale: The artefact is conditional on what the feature changes. Heuristic gaps are invisible in code review; the artefact is the only forcing function. The conditions are intentionally tight — over-application produces audit theatre.

rule.statement: When skipped (backend-only, API-only, data migration, internal refactor, build-system / CI / infra), readiness.md item 7 MUST be marked "no UI impact" with a one-line reason.
rule.rationale: Silent skip turns the gate into a rubber stamp. Explicit skip leaves an audit trail.

rule.statement: The Nielsen audit section in ui-ux-design.md MUST contain exactly these five rows: N1 visibility of system status, N3 user control & freedom, N4 consistency & standards, N5 error prevention, N6 recognition over recall. Adding rows for N2/N7/N8/N9/N10 is forbidden in this per-feature template.

rationale.source: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics, pruned by this methodology

rule.rationale: Bounded checklists get done; long checklists get faked. Five is the empirical sweet spot. N1, N3, N5, N6 catch the most common per-feature regressions (silent operations, no-cancel modals, validate-on-submit, wizards without breadcrumb context). N4 catches the cross-feature drift that explodes after enough small changes. The remaining five (match real world, error recovery, flexibility, aesthetic, help docs) are either site-wide concerns or rarely actionable per feature — they stay in education material because checking all 10 per feature is theatre.

rule.statement: Every clickable / tappable / focusable element MUST visually signal that it is interactive (cursor change, hover state, distinct visual treatment).
rule.rationale: Users do not hunt for hidden affordances. If a tile looks like a card and is also clickable, the click is invisible.

rule.statement: Hover effects MUST be applied ONLY to clickable elements. Decorative tiles MUST NOT hover-respond.
rule.rationale: Hover is an affordance signal — applying it to non-interactive elements lies to the user.

rule.statement: Every user action MUST produce visible acknowledgement within 100ms — at minimum a loading indicator, button press state, or focus change.
rule.rationale: Past 100ms the user repeats the click. Repeated clicks cause double-submit bugs and erode trust.

rule.statement: The six sections — Intent, Layout, States, Nielsen audit, Norman audit, Copy & microcopy — MUST appear in this order. Empty sections are filled with "n/a" and a reason, never omitted.
rule.rationale: Stable order + explicit n/a + reason makes the artefact diff-able across features.

rule.statement: The States section is a table with one row per state — empty, loading, error, success, disabled — and each row describes the visible affordance.
rule.rationale: Empty / loading / error / disabled are the states most often left unspecified, and they generate ~80% of post-launch UI bug reports. The table forces the author to name each one before code lands.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit ui-ux-design.md passing the output contract and tick readiness.md item 7.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when the feature touches UI and the artefact passes every shape check.

rule.statement: Skip; the feature is outside the SDD feature lifecycle or readiness.md item 7 is not in play.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.
